sections.title: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom

topics.title: The Sovereignty of God
items: God as Creator and Controller of the Universe (Gen. 1 and 2) cf. Amos 9:5-6; Is. 45:5-12 Ps. 19:1-6; Jer. 18:1-16; Rom. 8:28
objectives: i. define the term ‘sovereignty’
ii. analyse God’s process of creation
iii. interpret the sequence of creation
iv. identify man’s role in advancing God’s purpose in creation
v. recognize the sovereignty of God in the affairs of man and nations

topics.title: The Covenant
items: (a) The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
(c) God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11) cf. Deut. 28:1-19
objectives: i. explain the concept of covenant
ii. examine the importance and implication of the covenants
iii. distinguish between God’s covenants with Noah, Abraham and Israel
iv. Distinguish between the old and the new covenants

topics.title: Leadership Qualities
items: (d) Judges (Deborah - Judges. 4:1-24; Gideon: Judges 6:11-40; Samson : Judges 13:1-7, 21-25; 16:4-31)
objectives: i. examine the circumstances that gave rise to the leadership of Joseph, Moses, Joshua and the Judges
ii. identify the major talents of these leaders
iii. assess God’s role in the works of these leaders
iv. analyse the achievements of these leaders

topics.title: Divine Providence, Guidance and Protection
objectives: i. identify the different ways by which God guided and protected the people of Israel
ii. specify how God provided for His people
iii. identify the different occasions when God provided for Israel
iv. recognize that God still provides for people today

topics.title: Parental Responsibility
objectives: i. . determine the extent to which Eli, Samuel and David were responsible for the short-comings of their children
ii. describe how Asa pleased God

topics.title: Obedience and Disobedience
objectives: i. determine why Abraham, the Three Hebrew Youths and David obeyed God
ii. identify the rewards for obedience
i. compare the disobedience of Adam, the people of Israel, Moses and Saul
ii. indicate the reasons for their disobedience
iii. identify the consequences of disobedience

topics.title: A man after God’s own heart
items: (b) David’s submission to the will of God
(c) David’s repentance and forgiveness (II Sam. 11; 12:1-15, cf. Ps. 51:130)
objectives: i. identify David’s anointing experience
ii. specify how David submitted to the will of God
iii. examine the situations that led to David’s sin and repentance
iv. identify the consequences of David’s sin
v. identify why God forgave David

topics.title: Decision - Making
items: (c) Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (I Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
objectives: i. identify the source of Solomon’s wisdom
ii. compare the different ways used by Saul and Solomon in making decisions
iii. analyse the decisions made by Saul, Solomon and Rehoboam
iv. assess the consequences of Solomon and Rehoboam’s unwise decisions

sections.title: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

topics.title: Greed and its effects
objectives: iii. analyse the consequences of Ahab and Gehazi’s greed

topics.title: The Supremacy of God
items: Religious tension and the power of God on Mount Carmel (I Kings 16:29-34; 17:1-7; 18; 19:1-18)
objectives: i. assess the religious situation in Israel at the time of Elijah and Ahab
ii. identify the characters involved in the contest on Mount Carmel
iii. differentiate between God’s power and that of Baal

topics.title: Religious reforms in Judah
objectives: i. analyse Josiah’s religious reforms
ii. determine the reasons for the renewal of the covenant
iii. assess the significance of the reforms

topics.title: Concern for Judah
items: (c) Response to the state of Judah (Neh. 2; 4:1-23 Ezra 3:4; 5; 6; 7)
objectives: i. identify the reasons for the fall of Jerusalem
ii. examine the condition of Judah during the exile
iii. analyse the people’s response to the call of Nehemiah and Ezra to rebuild Jerusalem
iv. distinguish between Nehemiah and Ezra’s responses to the opposition of their enemies

topics.title: Selected Poems (Abụ Ndị A Họpụtara)
items: Faith, Courage and Protection Examples of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego (Dan. 3:1-30: 6:1-28

topics.title: God’s message to Nineveh
objectives: i. analyse the story of Jonah’s call
ii. describe the consequences of Jonah’s disobedience
iii. assess the effect of Jonah’s message on the Ninevites
iv. emulate the example of the Ninevites

topics.title: Social justice, True religion and Divine love
items: (a) Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14) cf James 1:19-27
objectives: i. determine what true religion is
ii. identify the ills that led to the call for social justice in Amos’ time
iii. identify the punishment meted for evil deeds
iv. examine the condition in Israel during Hosea’s time
v. analyse Hosea’s portrayal of divine love and human response

topics.title: Holiness and Divine call (Isaiah 6:1-13; Ezek. 2; 3:1-11; Jer. 1:4-10)
objectives: i. analyze the vision of Isaiah on God’s holiness
ii. distinguish the calls of Isaiah, Ezekiel and Jeremiah
iii. compare the assignments given to these prophets
iv. determine the need for God’s people to be holy

topics.title: Punishment and Hope
objectives: i. describe the situations that led to the punishment of Israel
ii. identify the conditions for hope
iii. determine the benefits of restoration

sections.title: Themes from the four Gospels and the Acts of the Apostles

topics.title: The birth and early life of Jesus
items: (b) The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18- 25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45;2 )
objectives: ii. assess the importance of John as the forerunner of Jesus
iii. describe the boyhood of Jesus

topics.title: The baptism and temptation of Jesus
objectives: i. determine the meaning and purpose of the baptism of Jesus
ii. enumerate the temptations of Jesus
iii. examine the significance of the temptations of Jesus
iv. describe how Jesus overcame the temptations

topics.title: Discipleship
objectives: i. identify the first disciples to be called by Jesus
ii. determine the demands of discipleship

topics.title: Miracles
items: (ii) Feeding of the five thousand (Mt. 14:13-24; Mk. 6:30-44; Lk. 9:10-17; Jn. 6:1-13)
(iii) Walking on the sea (Mt. 14:22-26; Mk. 6:45-52; Jn. 6:16-21)
(ii) The raising of Jairus’ daughter (Lk. 8:41-42, 49-56; Mk. 5:21-43)
(iii) The raising of the widow’s son at Nain (Lk. 7:11-17)
objectives: i. classify the different miracles of Jesus
ii. indicate the occasion of each of the miracles
iii. examine the significance of each of the miracles

topics.title: The Parables
items: (b) Parables about love of God (Mt. 18:12- 14; Lk. 15:1-32)
(c) Parables about love for one another (Lk.10:25-37; 16:19-31)
(d) Parable about wealth: The rich fool (Lk. 12:13-21)
objectives: i. define a parable
ii. classify the different parables of Jesus
iii. identify the occasion of each parable
iv. interpret the meaning of each parable
v. give reasons why Jesus taught in parables

topics.title: Sermon on the Mount (Mt. 5; 6; Lk. 6:17-26)
objectives: i. analyse the teachings on the Mount
ii. identify the demands of the Kingdom
iii. determine the consequences of placing worldly possessions above heavenly treasures
iv. associate the rewards for obedience with the Sermon on the Mount

topics.title: Mission of the disciples
items: (a)The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16) (b)The mission of the seventy (Lk. 10:1-24)
objectives: i. distinguish between the mission of the twelve and the seventy
ii. specify the instructions to the disciples
iii. assess the outcomes of the missions

topics.title: The Great Confession (Mt. 16:13-20; Mk. 8:27-30; Lk. 9:18-22)
objectives: i. analyse the confession by Peter
ii. identify the occasion of the Great Confession
iii. examine the significance of the Great Confession

topics.title: The Transfiguration (Mt. 17:1-13; Mk. 9:2-13; Lk. 9:28-36)
objectives: i. trace the events leading to the Transfiguration
ii. identify the personalities involved in the Transfiguration account
iii. determine the significance of the Transfiguration to the disciples

topics.title: The Triumphal Entry and the cleansing of the Temple (Mt. 21:1-17; Mk. 11:1-19; Lk. 19:29-48)
objectives: i. recount the Triumphal Entry and the cleansing of the Temple
ii. determine the significance of the Triumphal Entry and the cleansing of the Temple
iii. examine how the cleansing of the Temple caused hostility towards Jesus

topics.title: The Last Supper
objectives: i. trace the story of the Last Supper
ii. evaluate the significance of the Last Supper

topics.title: The trials and the death of Jesus
items: (b) Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
objectives: i. analyse the different trials of Jesus
ii. describe the crucifixion and burial of Jesus
iii. deduce the lessons of the death of Jesus
iv. recount the statements of Jesus on the cross

topics.title: Resurrection, appearances and ascension of Jesus
objectives: (i) trace the stories of the resurrection, appearances and ascension of Jesus
(ii) compare the personalities involved in the stories
(iii) analyse the relevance of the resurrection, appearances and ascension of Jesus

topics.title: Jesus’ teachings about
items: (a) The Bread of Life and the Living Water (Jn. 4:7-15; 6:25-58)
(c) The Door, the Lamb and the Good Shepherd (Jn. 1:29-34; 10:1-18)
objectives: (i) analyse the different teachings of Jesus about Himself
(ii) deduce the reasons for Jesus’ teachings about Himself
(iii) interpret the meanings of the symbols used by Jesus about Himself

topics.title: Love
items: (b) Love for one another (Jn. 13:34-35; 15:12-13; 1 cor. 13; cf. I Jn. 4:7-21)
objectives: (i) describe God’s love for man
(ii) identify various types of love
(iii) specify the ways they can love one another
(iv) evaluate the significance of love

topics.title: Fellowship in the Early Church
items: (b) Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11, 6:1-6)
objectives: (i) identify the reasons for communal living in the Early Church
(ii) identify the problems of communal living and their solutions
(iii) examine how communal living helped the growth of the Early Church

topics.title: The Holy Spirit and the mission of the Church
objectives: (i) trace the story of the Pentecost
(ii) identify the signs associated with the coming of the Holy Spirit
(iii) examine the significance of the Pentecost experience
(iv) analyse the mission of the Church

topics.title: Opposition to the Gospel message
items: (a) The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42 12:1-24)
objectives: (i) trace the story of the arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John
(ii) trace the events that led to the martyrdom of Stephen
(iii) describe the role of Saul in the persecution of the Church
(iv) evaluate the importance of persecution to the growth of the Church
(v) account for the persecution of Paul

topics.title: Mission to the Gentiles
items: (c) The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
objectives: (i) compare the conversions of Saul and Cornelius
(ii) analyse the commissioning and mission of Paul
(iii) examine the main decisions at the Council of Jerusalem
(iv) identify the personalities involved at the Council of Jerusalem
(v) examine the relevance of the main decisions at the Council of Jerusalem
(vi) assess Paul’s role in the mission to the Gentiles

topics.title: Justification by Faith
objectives: (i) interpret the phrase ‘justification by faith’
(ii) identify the basic conditions for justification
(iii) determine the fruits of justification

topics.title: The Law and Grace
objectives: (i) examine the purpose and significance of the law and grace
(ii) identify the place of the Law among the Jews

topics.title: New life in Christ
objectives: (i) describe the characteristics of the old life
(ii) analyse the new life in Christ
(iii) identify the conditions of the new life
(iv) examine the benefits of the new life

topics.title: Christians as joint heirs with Christ (Gal. 3:23-29; 4:1-7)
objectives: (i) describe how Christians are joint heirs with Christ
(ii) recognize that males and females are all children of God
(iii) indicate the benefits of being joint heirs with Christ

topics.title: Humility (Phil. 2:1-11; I Pet. 5:5-11) (James 4;10; Matt. 23:12)
objectives: (i) determine the meaning of humility
(ii) identify the requirements of humility
(iii) identify the rewards of humility

topics.title: Forgiveness (Philemon; II Cor. 2:5-11; Matt. 7;14-15)
objectives: (i) analyse Paul’s teaching on forgiveness
(ii) assess the benefits of forgiveness
(iii) recognize the need to forgive others

topics.title: Spiritual gifts
objectives: (i) identify the different spiritual gifts
(ii) analyse the benefits of spiritual gifts to the individual and the church
(iii) differentiate between spiritual gifts and talents

topics.title: Christian Giving
objectives: (i) interpret the concept of Christian giving
(ii) relate the teachings of Paul on Christian giving
(iii) identify the importance of Christian giving

topics.title: Civic responsibility (Rom. 13; I Tim. 2:1-4; 1Peter 2;13-17)
objectives: (i) identify the need for obedience to authority
(ii) specify the requirements of good citizenship

topics.title: Dignity of labour
objectives: (i) interpret the concept of dignity of labour
(ii) analyse the benefits of labour
(iii) recognize that no particular kind of work leads to loss of respect for personal dignity

topics.title: The second coming of Christ
items: a) The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; II Thess. 2:1-12) b) Preparation for His coming (Matt. 25;31-46; I Thess. 5:1-11; II Pet. 3:1-13)
objectives: (i) identify the signs of the Second Coming of Christ

(iii) indicate what will happen during His Second Coming
(iv) examine the importance of His coming

topics.title: Impartiality
objectives: (i) interpret the concept of impartiality
(ii) identify causes of partiality
(iii) examine the consequences of partiality

topics.title: Effective prayer
objectives: (i) identify the requirements of effective prayer
(ii) distinguish between effective and ineffective prayer
(iii) identify the importance of prayer
(iv) identify types of prayer

topics.title: Christian living in the community
items: (a) Interpersonal relationships among Christians (I Pet. 5:1-4; Rom. 12:3-21; 2 Pet. 1:3-11; Heb.13:1-21)
(d) Relationship in the Christian family (Eph. 6: 1-9; Col. 3:18-21
objectives: (i) determine interpersonal relationships among Christians

(iii) relate Christian attitude to persecution
(iv) determine the relationship in the Christian family

topics.title: Corruption
